## Goal

De-risk the arena's campaign integration (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A) before any build work: prove the shared campaign and upgrade-choice systems can run headless under Node/vitest with the same seed derivation the game uses, and identify every impure dependency so the design uses the shared core directly or a named thin adapter — never a divergent copy.

## Headline

A short spike that instantiates/runs the modules the arena will consume — `buildSequencedLevels` (src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts, all fixed/curve/dynamic modes), `sequencer`/`defaultCandidatePool` (src/core/difficultySequencer.ts), `WaveManager` (src/waves/WaveManager.ts), `chooseOptions`/`buildChoiceCandidates` (src/powerups/choice.ts), `MineralHold` (src/core/GameState.ts hold), and the hold-full reward application path (`applyMineralChoiceReward`, src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts) — and records exactly which are headless-pure and which need an adapter (e.g. the `EffectsRegistry` the reward applyer requires).

## Context

- The eval layer (src/ai/eval/) must stay pure: no wall clock, no I/O, no Phaser import.
- Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): an enabled behaviour runs the same code in gym/game and in the eval arena.
- Effort-and-risk unknowns recorded on the parent: can `sequencedLevels.ts` run headless without Phaser imports? Can the reward-application path be exercised without a Phaser `EffectsRegistry`?

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A vitest smoke test imports and exercises each target module without importing Phaser or a wall-clock/IO module in the eval entry path; the smoke test lives under src/ai/eval/ (e.g. a `campaignHeadless.test.ts` spike scaffold).
- **AC2:** Every impure dependency found is listed with a concrete adapter plan (thin, named, headless) or a recommendation to not model that behaviour in this item — recorded in a comment on this work item.
- **AC3:** The spike records the design decision the arena build follows: consume each shared entry point directly vs via the named adapter, with the seed derivation (createSeededRng + buildSequencedLevels {seed}) confirmed to be deterministic.
- **AC4:** The spike makes no production code changes outside src/ai/eval/ evaluation-only scaffolding; the finding is reproducible by a maintainer (commands recorded).

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic modes) to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — sequencer + candidate pool to prove headless-safe
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — wave/level state machine to prove headless-safe
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — shared upgrade-choice flow to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — MineralHold (capacity/growth/overflow)
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — applyMineralChoiceReward (EffectsRegistry dependency to assess)
- `src/ai/eval/campaignHeadless.test.ts` (new vitest spike scaffold) — headless-import smoke coverage
data.title: Spike: prove the shared campaign core runs headless (wave sequencer + upgrade choices)

# Produce and validate the promo, showreel and highlight clips

## Goal

Run the committed pipeline over the gathered footage to produce and validate
the actual deliverables and manifests: the ~45–60 s promo, the > 2 min
showreel, and several short highlight clips — all 960×540 WebM with the game's
SFX — accompanied by the selection and coverage manifests, and verify the
attention-grabbing pace criteria (AC1–AC4 of the parent).

**User story:** As the maintainer, I can share a compelling promo package that
opens with action and showcases weapons, pickups and enemies.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Deliverables produced.** `capture-output/` contains: the compiled
  promo WebM (~45–60 s), the showreel WebM (> 2 min), and several highlight
  clips — all at 960×540 with an audio track (VP9+Opus or VP8 fallback).
- **AC2 — Manifests produced.** The selection manifest (source WebM, series,
  mapped timestamps, motivating intensities) and the coverage manifest
  (feature → clip + timestamp ranges) accompany the deliverables; all three
  feature categories (weapons, pickups, enemies; boss when available) are
  listed.
- **AC3 — Pace verified.** The promo opens with action (no dead air in the
  first ~5 s) and cuts on peaks; verification measures the sampled non-black
  frame ratio and the average recorded intensity, and confirms they are at or
  above the documented reference band. The **reference band is documented**
  as part of this item (with the calibration basis).
- **AC4 — Per-clip intensities reported.** The manifest prints the per-clip
  recorded intensities so the pace claim is auditable.
- **AC5 — Validated.** Each deliverable passes the pipeline's validation step
  (decodable, non-trivial non-black pixels, audio present, correct resolution).

- **Covers parent AC1:** **AC1 — Deliverables at full game-native resolution.** The work produces, written under the gitignored `capture-output/` tree: (a) a single compiled promo WebM of ~45–60 s, (b) a longer showreel WebM (>2 min), and (c) several short highlight clips — all WebM (VP9+Opus or VP8 fallback) at the game's **full native 960×540 resolution** (the game renders natively at 960×540: `src/core/constants.ts`), each carrying the game's own SFX audio track.

## Key files

- `capture-output/` — gitignored deliverables + manifests
- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — the pipeline under test at runtime
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — reference band documented here

## Implementation notes

- This is a run/verify item: the *code* is delivered by the earlier items; this
  item executes the pipeline and records the evidence (file paths, durations,
  resolution, audio verdict, non-black ratio, mean intensity).
- If footage cannot evidence a category or the pace band is not met, record the
  gap explicitly and create a follow-up item rather than weakening the ACs.

## Deliverables

- The promo, showreel and highlight clips + both manifests + a pace report
  (comment on this item).

## Dependencies

- Depends on the ffmpeg driver (C5) and the gathered footage (C6).
data.title: Produce and validate the promo, showreel and highlight clips

# Test: wrapAware config plumbing

Test-first verification slice for the `wrapAware` parameter (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC1 + AC5). Pins the data-driven boolean's default, seed exclusions, CSV wiring and editor exposure **before** the implementation item lands, so the pipeline change is driven by failing tests.

## Goal

Pin the full config pipeline for `wrapAware`: default `true`, `march`/`centipede` seeded `false`, CSV persist + round-trip, editor-panel visibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts a generic archetype resolves `wrapAware === true` when the field is absent from its seed config.
- Tests assert the `march` and `centipede` seed configs carry `wrapAware === false` (the explicit exclusion list).
- A CSV round-trip test asserts a `wrapAware` column persists and reloads through the config CSV path; a missing/empty value falls back to `true`.
- A test asserts the field is enumerable through the existing `EnemyConfig` editor/config plumbing without extra per-field admin.
- All tests pass deterministically (no wall clock, no RNG).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts`
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts`
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`
- `src/utils/csvEdit.ts`
data.title: Test: wrapAware config plumbing

# Implement: wrapAware parameter pipeline

Implementation slice for the data-driven seam-awareness flag (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC1). Delivers the single per-archetype parameter that every later slice reads, so enabling or disabling seam-awareness is a one-field change.

## Goal

Add `wrapAware?: boolean` to `EnemyConfig`, default it to `true`, seed `march` and `centipede` to `false`, and persist it through the CSV and enemy editor panel.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `EnemyConfig` declares an optional `wrapAware?: boolean` with a doc comment stating the default (`true`) and the exclusion rationale.
- Seed defaults in `configDefaults.ts` yield `true` for every archetype except `march` and `centipede`, which are explicitly `false`.
- `enemy-configs.csv` gains a `wrapAware` column (documented in the CSV header comment block) with correct per-row values; empty values resolve to `true`.
- The enemy editor panel exposes the field so it is visible and editable.
- `BaseEnemy` (and/or the shared config plumbing) exposes the resolved flag to scenes via one accessor — no duplicated parsing.
- No gameplay behaviour changes in this slice; build and the changed-scope tests are green.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts`
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts`
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`
- `src/utils/csvEdit.ts`
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

- The parameter is the single source of truth for wrap-awareness; no hard-coded archetype key lists anywhere outside the seed defaults.

# Test: seam-aware aim angle

Test-first verification slice for seam-aware aimed fire (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC2 + AC5). Pins the shortest-wrapped-path aim maths before the shared aimed-fire seam changes, so the behaviour is specified by failing tests.

## Goal

Specify, in tests, that a wrap-aware enemy aims along the shortest **wrapped** path to the player while a non-aware enemy keeps the direct raw-position aim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unit test places a wrap-aware enemy near the left edge and the player near the right edge, and asserts the aim angle equals the wrapped-path angle (shot leaves the left edge, arrives from the right) — not the long direct angle.
- A unit test asserts that for a configuration where the direct line is already the shortest path, the wrapped angle equals the direct angle (no behaviour change mid-arena).
- A unit test asserts a non-aware enemy (`wrapAware: false`) keeps the current direct `atan2(target - position)` angle in the identical geometry.
- Tests cover both axes (horizontal seam and vertical seam) and the four-edge cases.
- The wrap maths is unit-tested independently of Phaser (pure function), matching the repo's pure-seam convention.
- All tests pass deterministically.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts`
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`
- `src/entities/Scout.ts`
- `src/entities/Scout.test.ts`
- `src/entities/enemyFire.test.ts`
data.title: Test: seam-aware aim angle

# Implement: seam-aware aimed fire

Implementation slice for seam-aware aimed fire (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC2). Every archetype routed through the shared aimed-shot method — Scout, `march` and the Raider — gains shortest-wrapped-path aiming in one place.

## Goal

Compute the player delta along the shortest wrapped path before `atan2` in the shared aimed-fire seam, gated on `wrapAware`, so shots can leave one edge and arrive from the opposite edge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The wrapped-delta calculation lives once in a shared pure helper in `src/scenes/core/` (or alongside `enemyTargeting.ts`) and is imported by the aimed-fire seam — no divergent copy in any entity.
- `Scout.tryFireAimedBullet` aims along the shortest wrapped path when `wrapAware` is true, preserving every existing gate (fire interval, shot probability, advance cue/tell, `shootEnabled`, alive, spawn guard).
- Aimed-fire archetypes sharing the method (`march`, `raider`) inherit the behaviour through the same seam with no per-class copy.
- An enemy with `wrapAware: false` keeps the current direct aim — bit-identical angles for mid-arena geometry.
- Radial/spread/burst patterns are untouched (out of scope per parent constraint).
- The bullet wrap model itself is untouched; only launch direction changes.
- Build passes and the changed-scope tests (including the slice-3 tests) are green.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Scout.ts`
- `src/entities/Raider.ts`
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts`

# Test: wrap-aware enemy movement

Test-first verification slice for wrap-aware movement (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC3 + AC5). Pins per-edge wrapping for wrap-aware archetypes and the unchanged bounded behaviour of the classic exclusions.

## Goal

Specify, in tests, that wrap-aware motion which would carry an enemy off-screen wraps to the opposite edge while `march` and `centipede` keep their bounded, wall-respecting behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests assert that crossing each of the four edges (left, right, top, bottom) relocates a wrap-aware enemy to the opposite edge, matching the player/asteroid four-edge wrap model (position only — velocity preserved).
- Tests cover the shared post-motion wrap helper in isolation (pure function, no Phaser) including the exact-boundary and multi-edge-overshoot cases.
- A test asserts `march` still reverses at the arena edge and drops vertically, and that `centipede` still weaves within bounds (`src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts` / centipede formation unchanged).
- A regression test asserts a non-aware archetype's position is never wrapped by the shared seam even when it leaves the arena bounds.
- At least one test covers each wrap-aware movement class (dive, chase, orbit, drift, roam, hold-and-move) at the seam.
- All tests pass deterministically.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
- `src/entities/Ghost.test.ts`
- `src/entities/Asteroid.test.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

- The tests fail against the pre-change bounded/clamped motion and pass once the shared wrap lands.

# Implement: shared post-motion edge wrap

Implementation slice for wrap-aware movement (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC3). One shared post-motion step wraps wrap-aware enemies across the seam instead of clamping them to the arena.

## Goal

Wrap each wrap-aware enemy's position in the shared scene entity loop (game + gyms), gated on `wrapAware`, so the whole wrapped playfield is the arena for every archetype except the classic exclusions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single shared post-motion wrap step lives in `src/scenes/core/` and is called from the shared entity loop used by both `PlayScene` and the gym scenes — no per-scene or per-entity copy.
- Wrap-aware enemies (dive, chase, orbit, drift, roam, hold-and-move) wrap across the opposite edge when their motion would carry them off-screen; velocity and heading are preserved (no reflection).
- `march` and `centipede` remain unchanged: march reverses and drops at the arena edge, centipede weaves within bounds.
- Formation bases and formation-shaping logic are unchanged — wrapping is entity-level only (per parent risk note).
- Steering that seeks the player remains stable near the seam (no oscillation); the shared wrap does not fight a steering state machine.
- No archetype other than the documented exclusions keeps bounded/clamped motion; any extra exclusion discovered is recorded as a code comment plus a documented divergence.
- Build passes and the changed-scope tests (including the slice-5 tests) are green.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
- `src/entities/Ghost.ts`
- `src/entities/Grunt.ts`
data.title: Implement: shared post-motion edge wrap

# Test: gym-game parity for wrap behaviour

Test-first verification slice for gym↔game parity (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC4 + AC5). Extends the repo-wide duplicate-body/parity guards to cover wrap-aware aim and motion so the game and every gym cannot drift.

## Goal

Prove, by test, that wrap-aware aim and movement run the *same* code in `PlayScene` and the affected gym scenes, and that the equivalence guards cover the new seams.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The parity/equivalence guard (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) covers the seam-aware aim and post-motion wrap seams and stays green.
- A cross-scene test asserts a wrap-aware aimed shot produces the same launch angle in the affected gym scene(s) and `PlayScene` for identical geometry.
- A cross-scene test asserts the post-motion wrap relocated position is identical in the affected gym scene(s) and `PlayScene`.
- Affected gym scenes (`GymFodderEnemies`, `GymCentipede`, and the shared `GymFormationScene`) are each exercised at least once for the wrap behaviour they host.
- A test asserts `GymCentipede` still shows bounded weaving (non-aware) while another gym shows seam wrapping (aware) — the divergence is asserted, not assumed.
- All tests pass deterministically.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts`

# Implement: wrap seams wired into PlayScene and gyms

Implementation slice wiring the shared wrap seams into the game and every affected gym (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC4). Makes the game and gyms consume the one shared implementation so parity holds by construction.

## Goal

Replace the remaining per-scene aim/motion call sites so `PlayScene` and each affected gym scene drive the shared seam-aware aim and post-motion wrap helpers, with no divergent copies left anywhere.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `PlayScene` and every affected gym scene (`GymFodderEnemies`, `GymCentipede`, the shared `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`) call the shared seam-aware aim and post-motion wrap helpers.
- The duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` reports no duplicated bodies for the new code.
- The gym-parity documentation assertion (`src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`) stays green.
- Any intentional divergence is limited to a *disabled feature* (non-aware archetypes), never a divergent copy.
- Build passes and the changed-scope tests (including the slice-7 tests) are green.

# Docs: wrapAware parameter and exclusions

Documentation slice for the seam-awareness feature (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC5). Records the parameter, the default, the exclusion list and the divergence rationale so tuning is a documented one-field change.

## Goal

Update the enemy design guide and any config-format documentation to describe `wrapAware`, its default, the `march`/`centipede` exclusions and the gym↔game parity obligation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` documents `wrapAware` (type, default `true`, effect on aimed fire and movement) and the rationale for the `march` and `centipede` exclusions.
- Any config-format documentation that enumerates `EnemyConfig` fields (including the CSV header comment block) lists `wrapAware` with its default and neutral-value semantics.
- The docs state the gym↔game parity obligation for future archetypes and the process for adding an exclusion (explicit seed-config entry, code comment, documented divergence).
- Documentation tests that assert on docs content stay green (`src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`, any enemy-roster docs tests).
- Written in UK English; no undocumented behaviour changes.

## Key Files

- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`
- `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`
